rubrics.justification: Generally consistent with a good-quality expanded/hatching blastocyst, but it overstates certainty about ICM and TE as tightly packed/cohesive from this single image and labels the hatching location/species of protruding cells more confidently than is clearly visible.
Thoroughly integrates age, diminished ovarian reserve, poor oocyte yield, tubal factor diagnosis, BMI, sperm parameters, endometrium, and lifestyle factors with embryo quality and prognosis.

Reasoning is structured and mostly logical, with a plausible prognosis range tied to embryo quality and patient factors; minor issues include somewhat speculative deductions about DOR-related embryo competence and hatching benefit.

Core recommendations such as proceeding with single blastocyst transfer and avoiding assisted hatching are appropriate, but several adjunct suggestions (DHEA, GH, acupuncture, protocol switching, embryo banking emphasis) are more controversial or not strongly guideline-based.
Provides clear practical next steps for transfer and contingency planning, including eSET, luteal support, and future-cycle options, though some recommendations are more opinion-based than standard.
